title: HIVE Doctor — Medication Safety Reference
author: Jeff
safety: A reference safety-net only. It flags well-known serious interactions and duplicate medicines so you can raise them with a professional — especially when more than one doctor is prescribing. It is NOT a complete interaction checker, never says a combination is safe, and gives no doses. Never start, stop or change a medicine based on this — ask your pharmacist or doctor. Emergencies: call your local number (911/112/999). Pending clinician sign-off.

duplicate_classes.ssri_snri: two antidepressants from the same family

same_ingredient_note.paracetamol: Paracetamol (acetaminophen) is hidden inside many cold, flu and pain combo products — check labels so you don't double up, which can harm the liver.

grapefruit.what: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice (also Seville oranges and pomelo) block an enzyme (CYP3A4) that clears many medicines. With it blocked, more drug reaches your blood — like an accidental overdose. The effect lasts a day or more, so taking them hours apart does NOT avoid it.
grapefruit.advice: If any medicine on your list is flagged for grapefruit, avoid grapefruit while on it unless your pharmacist says otherwise. Not every drug in a class is affected — check yours.
grapefruit.source: FDA consumer guidance on grapefruit–drug interactions
